title: What are you really selling?
principle: Sell what it means to them, not just what it is.

screens.text: Let me tell you about a washing powder. For years, washing powder ads in India promised spotless clothes. Then in 2005, Surf Excel said something strange: stains are good. "Daag acche hain."

screens.title: Stains are good
screens.text: In one ad, a little girl falls into a muddy puddle and cries. Her big brother jumps in and fights the puddle, to stand up for his sister. He gets very dirty, and the idea is simple: if a stain comes from doing something good, the stain is good.

screens.prompt: Every powder said "removes stains". What do you think "stains are good" was really selling to parents?

options.label: A lower price than other powders

screens.why: It sold a kind of parent: one who lets children play, help and stand up for others. Every powder removed stains. Only Surf said what that means for your child.

screens.title: Means–end laddering
screens.text: Marketers call this a means–end ladder. Think of a ladder with three steps. The bottom step is a feature: what it is or does. The middle step is a benefit: what that lets you do. The top step is a value: what it means to you.

screens.title: Surf's ladder
screens.text: Surf's ladder: it removes tough stains, the feature. So children can play freely, the benefit. So you're a parent who lets them do good, the value. Buyers compare features, but they choose values. And the top step only works if the bottom step is true.

screens.title: Now look at your business
screens.text: Washing powder and cakes seem far apart, but your bakery has a ladder too. It's mid-December. The butter videos kept your old buyers, but new buyers still compare your ₹850 with the chain shop's ₹700, even when your posts say "real butter".

screens.prompt: Here are three lines about your cake, mixed up. Put them in ladder order, from the bottom step to the top.
steps: Fresh, and safe for your child to eat
A birthday made at home, with love
screens.why: Well done. Real butter is what it is. Safe for your child is what that lets you do. A birthday made with love is what it means. Families choose with the top step, but only when a true fact holds it up.

screens.prompt: Which line should your New Year post use?

options.label: "Real butter, no preservatives, eggless, fresh daily"
"Real butter, no preservatives: made like home"
"Made with love, like a cake from home"

screens.why: Exactly. The fact makes the feeling true, and the feeling makes the fact matter. That's the whole ladder in one line.

wrong.a: All true, but only the bottom step, and facts get compared on price. The chain says "butter" too. Join the fact to what it means: "Real butter, no preservatives: made like home."
wrong.c: A feeling with no fact under it sounds empty, because any shop can say it. Join them: "Real butter, no preservatives: made like home."

screens.prompt: A chain shop's ad says, "Baked with a mother's love." Its cakes are made in a factory, with preservatives. What's wrong?

options.label: Nothing, because every ad talks like this
It should talk about its low price
Its cake can't back up the feeling

screens.why: Yes. A top step with nothing true under it is empty. Buyers who notice stop believing the shop.

wrong.a: Many ads do, and that's why buyers stop believing them. A feeling needs a true fact under it. A factory cake with preservatives can't back up "a mother's love".
wrong.b: Price is just another bottom step that rivals can beat. The real problem: the feeling isn't true, because a factory cake with preservatives can't back it up.

screens.prompt: I'll show you six lines about a cake. For each one, tell me: does it say what it is or does, or what it means?

items.text: A birthday your child will remember
Your child's happiest day of the year
Share sweet moments with the people you love

screens.why: Butter, eggless and no preservatives say what the cake is. A birthday to remember, a happiest day and shared moments say what it means. The best line joins one of each.

screens.setup: It's mid-December. New Year parties are coming. The chain shop sells cakes at ₹700; yours are ₹850 and leave you ₹450 each. Your next post goes to 500 past buyers.
screens.question: What does it say?

options.label: "Real butter, eggless, no preservatives. ₹850."
options.outcome: Families agree it's good, then compare ₹850 with ₹700. 12 order, leaving you ₹5,400.
options.why: True facts, but only the bottom step. Facts get compared on price.
options.better: Join the facts to what they mean: "Real butter, no preservatives: New Year, made like home."

options.label: "₹100 off this week only, real butter cakes!"
options.outcome: 14 order at ₹750, leaving you ₹350 each: ₹4,900. In January, families wait for your next offer.
options.why: You moved the talk to price, the one thing the chain shop wins on.
options.better: Join the facts to what they mean: "Real butter, no preservatives: New Year, made like home."

options.label: "Real butter, no preservatives: New Year, made like home"
options.outcome: Families reply with photos of last year's party at home. 20 order at ₹850, leaving you ₹9,000. Nobody asks about the chain shop's price.
options.why: A true fact carried a value families care about. They chose the value, not the cheaper cake.

screens.title: The honest line
screens.text: The line again: use on others only what you'd accept being used on you. Climb the ladder only on true steps. A feeling your product can't back up, like "a mother's love" on a factory cake, is a trick buyers will see through.
Sell what it ___ to them, not just what it ___.
screens.why: Exactly. Surf sold children who stand up for others, not just clean clothes. You sell a party made like home, on top of real butter.

summary: A means–end ladder: feature (what it is or does) → benefit (what that lets you do) → value (what it means).
Buyers compare features, but choose values. Join the two in one line.
Every step must be true. A feeling with nothing true under it is a trick.

cards.front: "99.7% pure ghee" or "Pure, like home". Which sells more?
cards.back: Buyers choose what it means to them, not just what it is.

cards.front: "Removes tough stains" is which step of the ladder?
cards.back: Feature: what it is or does. Benefit: what that lets you do. Value: what it means.

cards.front: A factory cake says "made with a mother's love". What's wrong?
options: No true fact backs up the feeling
cards.back: Climb the ladder only on true steps.

sources.label: Surf Excel's Daag Acche Hai campaign (Social Samosa, 2018)
